items.stem: New rows added to the source are missing from a PivotTable's results. What is the most robust fix?

options.text: Base the PivotTable on an Excel Table so the range expands automatically
options.rationale: Correct: a Table reference grows with the data, so refresh captures new rows.

options.text: Manually widen the range after every change
options.rationale: That is error-prone and easy to forget.

options.text: Delete and rebuild the pivot each time
options.rationale: Unnecessary and inefficient compared with a Table source.
GETPIVOTDATA is unrelated to the source range growing.

items.explanation: Correct: a Table reference grows with the data, so refresh captures new rows.

items.stem: Which TWO habits keep PivotTable analysis trustworthy? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Refresh the pivot after the source data changes
options.rationale: Correct: pivots do not update until refreshed.

options.text: Cross-check a key total against an independent SUM or count
options.rationale: Correct: an independent check catches grouping or double-counting mistakes.

options.text: Assume the Grand Total is always correct
options.rationale: Grand totals can mislead with blanks or double counting.

options.text: Hide subtotals so numbers look cleaner regardless of accuracy
options.rationale: Hiding detail does not make a wrong number right.

items.explanation: Correct: pivots do not update until refreshed.

options.text: Some source rows have empty or non-date values in the date field
options.rationale: Correct: blanks or text in the date column fall outside the date groups.

options.text: PivotTables always add a blank row
options.rationale: A '(blank)' appears only when the field actually contains blanks.
